<reason>Both sides ran disciplined, well-shaped cases. B's analytic spine ("aggressive is not accurate," aggression at scale means automation, punishment is regressive because throwaways lose nothing and invested accounts lose everything) produced the debate's sharpest single turn: A's triage answer was reframed as "PRO's triage doesn't answer my case; it maps it," which genuinely damaged A's human-review promise. B also handled A's contradiction question honestly ("both, for different people") and converted it into the regressivity argument. But B's route leaned on two under-defended links. First, B asserted that the severe categories A actually cares about — slurs, threats, sexual harassment, doxxing — are "already at ten on every major platform," which is precisely the empirical premise A's opening denied and which B never supported; that assertion is what makes B's "the motion's only marginal product is the ambiguous middle" narrowing work, so the narrowing never fully closes. Second, B never met A's open challenge to name a real player punished for genuine spontaneity rather than abuse, leaving the culture-chill harm hypothetical while A's silent-exit harm stayed intuitive. A also landed a real bind: B's own remedies (default-off voice, verification gates, rate limits, behavior-sorted matchmaking) are platform intervention imposed over exactly the "you're sanitizing our game" objections the motion tells us to override, and B's "a setting isn't a verdict" line blunts but does not dissolve it — especially since B quietly slid from "quarantine the reported" to "quarantine new accounts." A's closing offered the cleanest decision rule (when the platform is unsure, whose risk does it carry — the appealable veteran or the girl whose exit is uncounted), and pre-empted B's "don't guess at all" by showing inaction is itself a choice. B also paid an execution cost: three turns were clipped over the cap, cutting its concluding weighing each time. Thin but real edge to A.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's turn on A's triage concession — "humans go to the cases already enforced today, the ambiguous middle goes to the machine; PRO's triage doesn't answer my case, it maps it" — was the most damaging single strike. A's best counter was showing B's own toolkit (verification gates, default-off voice, behavior-based matchmaking) is platform intervention imposed over the very culture objections the motion asks us to override, leaving B without a defense of the players named in the motion.</best_rebuttal>
